small_guidance:
- Switch to NHWC (channels_last) layout for x and output so the IC inner loop coalesces across the channel axis; cast weight to (OC, KH, KW, IC) layout to match. This turns the current strided IC gather into contiguous vector loads.
- Add autotune configs with BLOCK_N=32/BLOCK_OC=256 and BLOCK_N=64/BLOCK_OC=128 at num_warps=4/8, num_stages=2, since OC=64 makes BLOCK_OC=64 a single tile per N and tile-N is the dominant axis (N*OH*OW ≈ 2M).
- Hoist the bias load outside any loop (already done) and fuse the hardswish+relu into a single `tl.maximum(tl.minimum(x+3,6), 0) * x / 6` (when x>0, hardswish≥0, so the outer relu is redundant — drop it).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an im2col-style GEMM with proper K-blocking: K = IC*KH*KW = 72. Treat (N*OH*OW) as M and OC as N, and do a single K-loop of length 72 with implicit im2col index math, accumulating with `tl.dot` on BLOCK_M×BLOCK_K and BLOCK_K×BLOCK_N tiles. The current outer-product accumulation does not use tensor cores; using tl.dot on tf32 will be much faster.
- Adopt channels-last input/output and pre-permute weights to (KH, KW, IC, OC) at __init__ so the K dimension is contiguous in both x (per (n,oh,ow) row, channels are contiguous) and W. Cache the permuted weight as a buffer to avoid per-call reshape.
- Consider a persistent-CTA design grouping by (n, oh-tile) so multiple (kh,kw) taps reuse loaded x rows across OC tiles; alternatively merge the kh/kw loops into one K loop iterating 0..KH*KW*IC and load BLOCK_K=32 contiguous channel slices per step, masking K-tail.
